summary: In the Rift Valley 1.5 km SE of Tamar 9. TE and TM split (2D effect of the fault). Near-surface 15-30 ohm.m for periods < 0.1 s, then a strong decrease (possibly < 6 ohm.m) of unknown thickness, over a resistive layer seen at 100-1000 s.
notes: The report gives only a qualitative interpretation; no 1D model.

summary: 3 km W of Tamar 9, near the steep flank of the Hatsera anticline. Anisotropic; TE/TM differ strongly below 10 s and converge at long periods.
notes: The report gives only a qualitative interpretation; no 1D model.

summary: 3 km W of Tamar 9. Anisotropic but less than TR-2 at short periods; TE/TM converge at long periods.
notes: The report gives only a qualitative interpretation; no 1D model.

summary: 3 km W of Tamar 9. Strongest anisotropy; TE apparent resistivity an order of magnitude below TR-2/TR-3, possibly a local low-resistivity anomaly (not confirmed).
notes: The report gives only a qualitative interpretation; no 1D model.
